facts.text: Quanah was founded in the 1880s as a railroad stop and named after Comanche chief Quanah Parker, son of Peta Nocona and Cynthia Ann Parker.
The 1908 Hardeman County Courthouse, a Beaux Arts building, sits beside a granite monument honoring Quanah Parker.
The 1890 stone Hardeman County Jail Museum, now a National Register site, tells the story of Quanah Parker and early settlers.
A 1938 mural by artist Jerry Bywaters at the post office chronicles Quanah’s history from buffalo plains to the 1930s.
Quanah’s name honors the last principal chief of the Comanche Nation, making it one of Texas’s few towns named for a Native American leader.
